title: zealandia pustulata subsp. howensis
intro: Zealandia pustulata subsp. howensis, commonly known as Howea forsteriana or the Sentry Palm, is a species of palm tree native to Lord Howe Island in Australia. This plant is used in traditional medicine, particularly in Australia and New Zealand, for its potential health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties. The therapeutic actions of Zealandia pustulata subsp. howensis include soothing skin irritations, reducing inflammation, and promoting wound healing, making it a popular ingredient in topical creams and ointments. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, saponins, and phenolic compounds, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and provide relief from various health issues.
